text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Wednesday it will support a plan to reorganise state-run Lithuanian Energy by passing responsibility for the heating sector to municipalities.
The government's press office said in a statement that it would authorise its representative to vote for the plan at the company's upcoming shareholders' meeting.
The press office said that the move was necessary to decentralise the country's inefficient and costly energy sector.
The government intends to divide the domestic heating arm of Lithuanian Enegy into six regional and 10 district companies controlled by local municipalities.
The new companies are expected proportionally assume part of Lithuanian Energy's share capital, profit or losses and legal financial obligations as of May 1, 1997.
The current share capital of Lithuanian Energy stands at 2.8 billion litas and it is expected that it will amount to 1.8 billion litas after the reorganisation.

Lithuanian Energy said earlier that in the first quarter of 1997 it suffered 49.1 million litas of losses from operating the heating sector while electric energy production yielded 47.1 million litas in profit.
